7.Title: Acute coronary syndrome with unstable presentation
KeyIssues: The role of percutaneous mechanical circulatory support (MCS) devices in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and cardiogenic shock (CS) remains unclear.
RecommendedResearch: Randomized comparisons between standard of care and percutaneous MCS devices in ACS with CS.

8.Title: Management of acute coronary syndrome during hospitalization
KeyIssues: Clinical improvement through the use of risk stratification based on validated risk prediction models.
RecommendedResearch: Patients randomized to a particular intervention or to usual care based on validated risk prediction models to test clinical benefit of risk‑guided strategies.

9.Title: Technical aspects of invasive strategies
KeyIssues: Does intravascular imaging‑guided revascularization strategy improve clinical outcomes in patients with ACS?

Does intracoronary physiology assessment of myocardial reperfusion after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) improve risk stratification and/or enable stratified medicine to limit microvascular dysfunction and reperfusion injury/microvascular obstruction (MVO) post‑ACS?
In ACS patients with an infarct‑related artery (IRA) unsuitable for stent implantation, does drug‑coated balloon treatment of the IRA improve clinical outcomes?
Microvascular obstruction associated with PPCI is an unmet clinical need; therapies for prevention and treatment of MVO are urgently needed.
Does early implementation of MCS in management of high‑risk ACS patients improve clinical outcomes?
RecommendedResearch: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the efficacy of intravascular imaging‑guided revascularization strategies to improve meaningful clinical outcomes in ACS.
Prospective evaluation of whether intracoronary physiology assessment of myocardial reperfusion better stratifies patient risk.
Trials randomizing patients with an IRA unsuitable for stent implantation to drug‑coated balloon treatment versus usual care to evaluate clinical outcomes.
Preclinical and clinical research to evaluate cardioprotective therapies aimed at reducing microvascular obstruction.
RCTs evaluating the benefit of using MCS in high‑risk patients.
Randomized trials to determine whether intracoronary hypothermia reduces myocardial infarct size (further research text truncated on page).
